tr.td: A general clinical alert that does not fall into a more specific clinical category.
An alert concerning a known or suspected allergy or intolerance.
An alert concerning medication prescribing, dispensing, administration, duplication, or interaction.
An alert concerning vaccination eligibility, contraindication, due status, administration, or follow-up.
An alert concerning an abnormal, critical, pending, or otherwise significant laboratory result.
An alert concerning infection prevention, isolation, exposure, or transmission risk.
An alert concerning protection, abuse, neglect, exploitation, or another safeguarding risk.
An alert concerning a notifiable condition, outbreak, surveillance event, or public-health action.
An alert concerning an administrative, operational, eligibility, consent, or service-delivery issue.
An alert concerning record completeness, identity, duplication, integrity, or another data-quality issue.
An alert category not represented by another code in this code system.

div.p: Expansion performed internally based on codesystem Nigeria Alert Code System v0.0.0 (CodeSystem)

tr.td: A clinical contraindication relevant to a planned intervention, medication, immunization, or procedure.
A known or suspected allergy or intolerance risk requiring attention.
A possible clinically significant interaction involving one or more medications.
Potentially duplicative medication or treatment has been identified.
A scheduled medication or immunization dose was not administered as expected.
A scheduled medication or immunization dose is currently due.
A scheduled medication or immunization dose is overdue.
A clinical or diagnostic result is outside its expected or acceptable range.
A critical clinical or diagnostic result requires urgent review or action.
A clinically relevant diagnostic result is still pending.
An infection, exposure, or transmission risk requires attention or precautions.
The subject requires isolation or specific infection-prevention precautions.
A safeguarding concern requires review or protective action.
The subject may have more than one health record.
Demographic, biometric, or identifier information may not match the intended subject.
A data-quality, completeness, consistency, or record-integrity issue requires review.
A consent directive limits access, disclosure, or use of the subject's information.
The subject requires clinical, public-health, or administrative follow-up.
Referral to another provider, facility, service, or level of care is required.
A statutory, programmatic, or public-health report or notification must be submitted.
The subject's information or clinical status requires urgent review.
An alert type not represented by another code in this code system.

tr.td: The existence of the report is registered, but there is nothing yet available.
This is a partial (e.g. initial, interim or preliminary) report: data in the report may be incomplete or unverified.
Verified early results are available, but not all results are final.
The report is complete and verified by an authorized person.
Subsequent to being final, the report has been modified. This includes any change in the results, diagnosis, narrative text, or other content of a report that has been issued.
Subsequent to being final, the report has been modified to correct an error in the report or referenced results.
Subsequent to being final, the report has been modified by adding new content. The existing content is unchanged.
The report is unavailable because the measurement was not started or not completed (also sometimes called "aborted").

The authoring/source system does not know which of the status values currently applies for this observation. Note: This concept is not to be used for "other" - one of the listed statuses is presumed to apply, but the authoring/source system does not know which.

A highly specialized hospital offering advanced diagnostic, therapeutic, and surgical care, often affiliated with teaching or research institutions.

tr.td: Number of people living with HIV newly started on ART during the month, excluding ART transfer-in.
Number of people living with HIV currently receiving ART during the month.
Number of people living with HIV on ART for at least six months with a viral-load test result within the last 12 months.
Number of people living with HIV on ART for at least six months with virologic suppression of 1000 copies/mL or less within the last 12 months.
Number of people living with HIV on ART who had treatment interruption during the reporting month, disaggregated by tracking outcome.
Number of people living with HIV who restarted ART during the month.
Number of people living with HIV who transferred out during the month.
Number of people living with HIV who transferred in during the month.
Number of people living with HIV on ART with current health-insurance cover.
Number of people living with HIV on ART, including PMTCT clients, who were clinically screened for TB in HIV treatment settings.
Number of people living with HIV on ART with presumptive TB during the month.
Number of people living with HIV on ART with presumptive TB who were tested for TB during the month.
Number of people living with HIV on ART who had active TB disease.
Number of people living with HIV on ART with active TB disease who initiated TB treatment.
Number of people living with HIV on ART who initiated TB preventive treatment.
Number of people living with HIV on ART who completed a course of TB preventive treatment among those who initiated it.
Number of people living with HIV currently on ART who had ever received TB preventive treatment.
Number of people living with HIV newly enrolled in care during the month.
Number of people living with HIV with advanced HIV disease: WHO clinical stage 3 or 4, CD4 below 200 cells/mm3, or child aged five years or younger.
Number of people living with HIV with advanced HIV disease screened for serum cryptococcal antigen.
Number of people living with HIV with advanced HIV disease and positive serum CrAg who were screened for cryptococcal meningitis by lumbar puncture.
Number of people living with HIV started on treatment for cryptococcal meningitis.
Number of women living with HIV on ART screened for cervical cancer.
Number of women living with HIV on ART who screened positive, were eligible for treatment, and received cryotherapy, thermal ablation or LEEP.

div.p: Expansion performed internally based on codesystem ObservationStatus v4.0.1 (CodeSystem)
The existence of the observation is registered, but there is no result yet available.
This is an initial or interim observation: data may be incomplete or unverified.

The observation is complete and there are no further actions needed. Additional information such "released", "signed", etc would be represented using Provenance which provides not only the act but also the actors and dates and other related data. These act states would be associated with an observation status of preliminary until they are all completed and then a status of final would be applied.
Subsequent to being Final, the observation has been modified subsequent. This includes updates/new information and corrections.
Subsequent to being Final, the observation has been modified to correct an error in the test result.
The observation is unavailable because the measurement was not started or not completed (also sometimes called "aborted").

The authoring/source system does not know which of the status values currently applies for this observation. Note: This concept is not to be used for "other" - one of the listed statuses is presumed to apply, but the authoring/source system does not know which.

div.p: Expansion performed internally based on codesystem NG Vaccine contraindications CS v0.0.0 (CodeSystem)

tr.td: The individual has a weakened immune system due to a medical condition (e.g., cancer, organ transplant, or immunosuppressive therapy), which contraindicates certain live vaccines.
The individual is currently experiencing a severe febrile or respiratory illness (REFI), which may necessitate deferral of immunization until recovery.
The individual has a documented history of a severe allergic (anaphylactic) reaction to a previous dose of a vaccine or any of its components, making re-administration contraindicated.
The individual has symptomatic HIV infection, which may contraindicate live vaccines or require specific vaccine schedules based on immunological status.
